correctness.rationale: Let T:X→Y bounded and injective between real Banach spaces, C_T={(t,x):t≥||Tx||}. For any increasing net with upper bound, t_i↗s and ||Tx_j−Tx_k||≤2(s−t_i) above common predecessor i; Banach completeness produces image norm limit y. A candidate (u,w) is above every element iff u≥s+||Tw−y||: limit proves necessity, triangle inequality gives sufficiency. If y∈T(X), (s,T^{-1}y) is least; if a supremum (u,w) existed, compare it with q_i=(s+||Tx_i−y||,x_i), then u+||Tw−y||≤s and upper bound requires u≥s+||Tw−y||, forcing Tw=y. If T(X) nonclosed, choose a summably fast image approximating inaccessible y and let scalar increments equal successive image distances; resulting monotone bounded sequence has no supremum. Diagonal T on ℓ1, (Tx)_k=2^{-k}x_k, x_n=∑_{k≤n}e_k, t_n=1−2^{-n}, gives s=1 and y=(2^{-k}) with no ℓ1 preimage; (2,0) is a concrete order upper bound. All net quantifiers and closed-range equivalences verified directly.

value.rationale: Calculating every upper bound, not just existence of a supremum, distinguishes leastness from minimal upper bounds and shows precisely how nonclosed operator ranges obstruct monotone order completeness. This is a natural structural statement about closed generating nonnormal cones and gives a nontrivial uniform constructive counterexample for every nonclosed range, directly addressing a recognized gap in monotone-order Banach space geometry.

limitations: Injective bounded real Banach operator T only; no assertion of strong x_i convergence for nonclosed ranges.
Earlier pairwise quasi-supremum literature may contain analogous formulas under aliases, bounded search only.
